title: Chelsea’s Mayra Ramirez may miss rest of season after injury setback, Sonia Bompastor says
content:
Chelsea striker Mayra Ramirez may not play this season after picking up another injury during her rehabilitation, head coach Sonia Bompastor says.

Ramirez, 26, has not appeared for Chelsea this term since having surgery on a hamstring injury sustained in a pre-season game in August. She was initially slated to be out until the beginning of 2026 but has since suffered multiple setbacks.

“Mayra was progressing well, but she picked up a new injury in her rehab again,” Bompastor said in a press conference on Thursday. “It’s been a really tough and difficult season for her.

“I’m not sure we will see her until the end of the season, unfortunately.”

Bompastor continued: “(She’s) struggling mentally. That’s normal. I think it’s been a tough season for her with injuries. And sometimes it’s difficult to explain everything.

“I spoke with her yesterday. She’s really low right now. That’s normal. But everyone in the club is making sure we are supporting her in the right way, and we are providing her what she needs.”

Chelsea paid a then-world record fee of €450,000 plus €50,000 in add-ons to sign Ramirez from Levante in January 2024. She scored four goals in 17 Women’s Super League appearances last season.

Chelsea will also be without captain Millie Bright for Sunday’s women’s League Cup final against Manchester United, with Bompastor unable to provide a timeframe for the defender’s return. She said Bright’s recovery is taking “a little bit longer than what we expected.”

However, Bompastor confirmed that centre-back Nathalie Bjorn, who has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since December, will return to the squad. Fellow centre-back Kadeisha Buchanan returned from over a year out with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in Chelsea’s last game before the international break, a 2-1 victory over Manchester United in the FA Cup.

Full-back Niamh Charles (ankle) and forward Catarina Macario (heel), who have not appeared for Chelsea this year, remain unavailable and Bompastor could not provide timeframes for their return.

Chelsea will also be without striker Sam Kerr and full-back Ellie Carpenter on Sunday, who are on international duty with Australia at the Asian Cup.
